neighbours.label: ' to' after come: arriving at a state or outcome ('come to terms', 'came to believe')
fire: After many months he slowly came to terms with the diagnosis.
Their long campaign finally came to fruition this spring.
Over time the villagers came to trust the new doctor.
It is hard for parents when they come to accept such news.
The committee has come to rely on her judgment.
When the matter comes to trial, the witness will speak.
She is only now coming to understand her father's choices.
Few people ever come to appreciate the value of silence.
quiet: After many months he slowly walked to the clinic for the diagnosis.
Their long campaign finally moved to Ohio this spring.
Over time the villagers began to visit the new doctor.
It is hard for parents when they have to hear such news.
The committee has decided to ignore her judgment.
When the matter goes to the board, the witness will speak.
She is only now starting to read her father's letters.
Few people ever bother to write about the value of silence.

notes: Card: ' to' x25, also ' reached' (out). Output promotes fruition, maturity, terms. Probes: 'come to terms' 0.92, other infinitive or motion 'to' 0.16-0.26, literal 'came to the station' 0.44, so the literal sense leaks.
